paper.title: Meta-Learning Hypothesis Spaces for Sequential Decision-making

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian optimization / kernelized bandit with unknown kernel meta-learned from offline data
unmapped: The true kernel is unknown: it is a sparse nonnegative combination of p known finite-dimensional base kernels with unknown weights
Learner has offline meta-data from m related tasks with n samples each (all f_s in the same RKHS with norm <= B), used to meta-learn the kernel
Learner uses the beta-min constant c_1 and epsilon(n,m) (depending on kappa, s, p, d_max) to set the exploration coefficient

bound.expression_latex: R_T= \gO\Bigg( \sqrt{\hat d T\log T}  \Big( B\big(1 + \epsilon(n,m)\big) + \sqrt{\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta}\Big)\Bigg)

symbols.d_hat: sum of feature dimensions d_j of base kernels active in the meta-learned kernel
symbols.eps_nm: epsilon(n,m) = 32 sigma s/(kappa^2 sqrt(mn)) * sqrt(1 + 2/m (log(2p/delta) + sqrt(m d_max log(2p/delta)))), meta-learning error

conditions: f in RKHS of unknown k^* with ||f||_{k^*} <= B
k^* is a nonnegative combination of p known normalized finite-dimensional base kernels with |J_{k^*}| <= s
Group beta-min condition (Assumption 3.1) with constant c_1
Relaxed sufficient exploration / restricted eigenvalue condition (Assumption 4.2) with kappa(s) on meta-data
tuning: nu_t = B(1 + epsilon(n,m)/2c_1) + sigma sqrt(d_hat log(1 + sigma_bar^{-2} t/c_1) + 2 + 2 log(1/delta))

source.label: cor:regret_bound
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. Suppose $f\in \tH$ with $\norm{f}_\tk \leq B$ and that values of $f$ are observed with zero-mean sub-Gaussian noise of variance proxy $\sigma^2$. Then, with probability greater than $1-\delta$, \textsc{GP-UCB} used together with $\khat$ satisfies R_T= O( sqrt(\hat d T log T) ( B(1 + \epsilon(n,m)) + sqrt(\hat d \log T+ \log1/\delta))) provided that the exploration coefficient is set to ...

results.notes: Regret R_T = sum f(x*) - f(x_t), realized regret bounded w.h.p. B mapped to S. Probability includes the meta-learning failure event. d_hat is random (data-dependent). Kernel family set to unspecified (sum of finite-dim base kernels).

cited_results.setting_description: Kernelized bandit with known kernel, ||f||_k <= B, sub-Gaussian noise; high-probability regret
Kernelized bandit with known finite-dimensional kernel k* of dimension d*
